properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Posture control in the explorer's ethpool-bridge API: the request signature is an HMAC-SHA256 digest (hmacSign, handlers/api.go:3399) and RegisterEthpoolSubscription compares it with plain != at handlers/api.go:3355. Timing leak on an attacker-supplied authenticator; fix is hmac.Equal/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare. All other 27 regex hits were pagination/emptiness/nil checks and were rejected as false matches.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hardcoded secrets committed to the repo: JWT signing secrets and session secrets in config.yaml:20, config-example.yml:24, config/default.config.yml:26 and local-deployment templates/provisioning scripts (explorer-config-template.yml:45/46/54, provision-explorer-config.sh:85/86/94), plus a 32-byte hex private key in local-deployment/scripts/deposit_validator.sh:28. The '1111…'/'0123…' values are placeholder-style defaults, but they are real credential material the shipped config consumes (golang

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: User-account password hashing for the explorer frontend: bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword with cost 10 on registration/password-set (db/frontend.go:116, handlers/auth.go:100) and bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword on login/verify (handlers/auth.go:300, handlers/user.go:1182,1282). Cost 10 is the library default; quantum exposure is only Grover's square-root on the 184-bit effective strength, so rating C is fair. Provided by golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt (go.mod, same declaration as LIB-3e1cc194).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Math.random() in vendored frontend bundles served by the explorer UI: Bootstrap's getUID element-id prefixes (bootstrap.js/bootstrap.bundle.js) and Highcharts wordcloud placement jitter. Real non-cryptographic PRNG uses in shipped third-party JS, but in UI contexts — no key, token, or session-secret generation found in the frontend code.

components.name: Go crypto/tls sessions on default settings (Go 1.23.1)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All outbound HTTPS of the explorer (beacon/execution node RPC at rpc/erigon.go:77 and rpc/lighthouse.go:1319, ClickHouse, Bigtable remote store, Dune, defillama/coin-pricing, reCAPTCHA verification, Rocketpool, monitoring webhooks, Stripe email updater) goes through http.Client on Go 1.23.1 defaults. Verified basis: go.mod pins go 1.23.1; crypto/tls then negotiates TLS 1.3 with x25519 as weakest/default group — X25519MLKEM768 only becomes default in Go 1.24, and the offered X25519Kyber768Draft00

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Three live SHA-256 uses: (1) handlers/api.go:3399 as the hash inside HMAC-SHA256 request signing (ethpool bridge); (2) services/notifications.go:702 digest stored as unsubscribe_hash for notification unsubscribe links; (3) utils/eth.go:137 EIP-4844 blob versioned-hash (VersionedBlobHash) for blob-carrying transactions. SHA-256 is quantum-safe against practical attack (Grover square-root only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 capability shipped by the declared @noble/hashes@1.8.0 dependency (package-lock.json). This is the dependency inventory: the frontend build ships SHA-256 via this package whether or not the app's own code calls it directly. Changeable here by bumping the package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3-256 capability shipped by the declared @noble/hashes@1.8.0 dependency (package-lock.json) — same provider as the SHA-256 entry ALG-928ac765. Dependency inventory: the build ships this primitive via the package whether or not the app calls it directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-provided SHA-3/Keccak in the shipped frontend bundle: @noble/hashes@1.8.0 declares sha3 in package-lock.json. The frontend JS (shard-1 static/) is where noble's hashes would be reached (eth2 keytool/deposit/BIP39 code paths); presence in the lockfile means the algorithms ship with the build regardless of individual call sites.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA256 request signing for the ethpool bridge (hmacSign at handlers/api.go:3398-3402): signs "ETHPOOL <pkg> <user_id>" for subscription registration and mints "BEACONCHAIN <user_id>" receipt strings; key from Config.Frontend.BeaconchainETHPoolBridgeSecret (config-sourced, GCP Secret Manager compatible). Note the verification side compares the digest with != (see ALG-99c6681d). HMAC-SHA256 remains quantum-adequate; CNSA 2.0 environments would move to HMAC-SHA-384.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Key-management infrastructure: ProcessSecrets (utils/gdecoder.go:36-60) walks the config struct and replaces any field whose value starts with "projects/" by fetching it from Google Cloud Secret Manager (secretmanager.NewClient at :181, AccessSecretVersionRequest at :187). Production deployments can keep the JWT signing secret, ethpool HMAC secret, CSRF auth key and Stripe webhook secret out of config.yaml this way. Secret access is via the runtime's ADC credentials; the store's own envelope/CMK

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same logical asset as LIB-17b49471: the jwt/v4 module recorded by the algorithm scanner. The JWT signing capability is fed by the hardcoded jwtSigningSecret in config.yaml; HMAC-based signing is the default path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto declared in go.mod and used by first-party code (e.g. handlers/auth.go) — provides bcrypt password hashing for user authentication and the wider x/crypto primitive set. Version pinned in go.mod; the shipped bcrypt cost is what protects the password verifiers (see the bcrypt object ALG-2384a3f4, judged by the other scout).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes@1.8.0 declared in package-lock.json — JS crypto library shipped in the frontend build; provides the SHA-256 (ALG-928ac765) and BLAKE3 (ALG-979eccf8) primitives recorded as separate algorithm facets of this same provider. Dependency inventory: presence is what this entry records; the app's own TS may reach it via a bundler.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: github.com/pion/dtls/v2@v2.2.12 pinned in go.sum — DTLS handshake library used for WebRTC data channels (pulled in with pion/webrtc; the LIB-484ecd4e/LIB-a5adb62f records are judged by the other scout). DTLS 1.2 negotiates classical ECDHE key exchange — harvestable traffic once quantum hardware matures; observable here, replaceable upstream by pion. No first-party DTLS call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: DTLS-SRTP is the mandatory key exchange/security layer pion/webrtc/v3@v3.3.0 provides for WebRTC media; declared in go.sum. No first-party WebRTC call site found in the application — the algorithms ship in the module graph (available in the shipped library; no call site found in the application). pion's DTLS 1.2/1.3 handshake uses classical ECDHE curve negotiation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: golang.org/x/crypto@v0.32.0 is a direct dependency; the only subpackage the application imports is bcrypt (db/frontend.go:18, handlers/auth.go:21, handlers/user.go:34 — see ALG-2384a3f4). The module also ships ssh, openpgp, acme and other algorithm surfaces that are available to the build but not invoked first-party; recorded as the shipped extended-crypto provider at v0.32.0.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto/rand (imported as securerand at utils/utils.go:6) backs GenerateRandomBytesSecure (:1058) → RandomString and GenerateRandomAPIKey (:1192, securerand.Int over a 62-letter alphabet, base64url-encoded) — the user API keys for the explorer's API. CSPRNG use is correct practice; kept as the inventory's randomness asset.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: github.com/quic-go/quic-go@v0.48.2 pinned in go.sum — QUIC transport (TLS 1.3-based key exchange, classical X25519/ECDHE groups) in the module graph as a transitive dependency. Observable here, replaceable upstream; no first-party QUIC session setup found. quic-go v0.48 does not offer ML-KEM hybrid key exchange.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: github.com/miekg/dns@v1.1.62 in go.sum — DNS library with DNSSEC validation/signature support (ECDSA P-256, RSA, Ed25525/Ed448 algorithm registries) in the module graph as a transitive dependency. DNSSEC chain-of-trust signatures are Shor-vulnerable; observable here, replaceable upstream. No first-party DNSSEC call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v3.2.2+incompatible — ACTIVELY imported by utils/oauthutils.go, where it signs and verifies the explorer's session JWTs with HS256 (see the JWT HS256 finding at utils/oauthutils.go:38-88). Not merely an indirect dependency. Legacy major version; v5 of golang-jwt is current. Changeable here by migrating the import path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4@v4.5.1 — used by exporter/appsubscription_oracle.go to hold/parse Apple's JWS signed-transaction claims (client.ParseNotificationV2 via the awa/go-iap library) and pulled in by that library as well. Distinct from the v3 module that signs the app's own session JWTs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: github.com/quic-go/quic-go@v0.48.2 in go.sum (transitive, via the pion/webrtc stack). QUIC's handshake is TLS 1.3 with classical (x25519/ECDHE) key establishment; available in the shipped module graph, no first-party QUIC call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: github.com/pion/dtls/v2@v2.2.12 in go.sum (transitive via pion/webrtc/v3). Implements the DTLS 1.2/1.3 handshake with classical ECDHE key exchange and the standard cipher suites; shipped in the module graph, no first-party DTLS call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: github.com/pion/webrtc/v3@v3.3.0 in go.sum — WebRTC stack whose media path mandates DTLS-SRTP (see ALG-176654c7) and pulls pion/dtls/v2 and quic-go into the module graph. Available in the shipped library; no first-party call site found in the application.
